tagline: The Full Moon Party island at Haad Rin, plus Than Sadet waterfall, quiet northern beaches, and the Srithanu wellness scene
introHtml:
Koh Phangan sits in the middle of the Gulf of Thailand, in Surat Thani province, between Koh Samui and Koh Tao. The world knows it for the Full Moon Party at Haad Rin, a beach party held every month on the night of the full moon. But Phangan has plenty of other sides that most people never see.

The north and west of the island are calm and quiet, with white-sand beaches like Bottle Beach (reachable only by boat), Koh Ma off Mae Haad where you can snorkel over coral, and Than Sadet waterfall inside the national park, once visited by Thai kings. The Srithanu area has become a hub for yoga, wellness, and health cafes where people stay for weeks. Thong Sala is the island's main pier and market town. You can come to Phangan to party, to find quiet, or to rest and recharge.
bestTime: December–April: clear seas, gentle waves, ideal for swimming, snorkeling, and reaching the northern beaches. The Full Moon Party runs every month, so check the full-moon date before booking. October–November is rainy with rough seas.

highlights.name: Full Moon Party, Haad Rin
highlights.blurb: The world-famous beach party held every month on the night of the full moon at Haad Rin. People come from all over to dance on the sand all night, and it's the first thing most travelers picture when they hear Koh Phangan.

highlights.name: Haad Rin
highlights.blurb: The twin beaches at the southern tip of the island, with the lively Haad Rin Nok and the quieter Haad Rin Nai. This is the island's hub for hotels, restaurants, and beachfront bars.

highlights.name: Than Sadet Waterfall
highlights.blurb: A waterfall inside Than Sadet–Koh Phangan National Park, once visited by Thai kings, with royal initials carved into the rocks. A short trek leads to pools where you can swim.

highlights.name: Bottle Beach
highlights.blurb: A quiet white-sand beach on the north coast, reachable by boat or on foot. The water is clear and the crowds are thin, making it a dream beach for anyone wanting to escape the bustle.

highlights.name: Koh Ma, Mae Haad
highlights.blurb: A small island off the northwest tip, linked to Mae Haad by a sandbar you can walk across at low tide. It's the best snorkeling spot on the island for seeing coral.

highlights.name: Srithanu, Wellness and Yoga
highlights.blurb: The west-coast area packed with yoga studios, wellness retreats, and vegan cafes. People stay for weeks here to recharge and catch the sunset.

foodScene.name: Fresh Seafood
foodScene.note: As a fishing island, Phangan has shrimp, shellfish, crab, and fish straight off the boats. Beachfront seafood spots grill, steam, stir-fry with curry powder, and make tom yum to eat by the water.

foodScene.name: Thong Sala Night Market
foodScene.note: The night market in the Thong Sala pier area gathers Thai and southern street food, grilled and fried dishes, sweets, and fruit, at friendlier prices than the tourist beaches.

foodScene.name: Srithanu Health and Vegan Cafes
foodScene.note: The wellness area has plenty of vegan cafes, smoothie bowls, and clean food, ideal for the health-minded staying long term. Sit back and take in the west-coast sea view.

foodScene.name: Beach Bars and Buckets
foodScene.note: Haad Rin and the tourist beaches have beach bars, cocktail buckets, and live music, the seaside party scene the island is known for. Drink responsibly and keep an eye on your valuables.

foodScene.name: Bold Southern Food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, gaeng lueang, stir-fried stink beans (pad sataw), and khao yam turn up at local spots around the island, packing the fierce southern punch that goes with hot rice.

foodScene.name: Coffee and Brunch
foodScene.note: Fresh-coffee cafes and brunch spots are spread across both Srithanu and Thong Sala. Easy places to work or take a break before heading out to the beach.

foodScene.name: International Restaurants
foodScene.note: With so many foreign visitors, the island has Italian, Mexican, Indian, and Mediterranean restaurants to switch things up, especially around Haad Rin and Srithanu.

foodScene.name: Island Fruit and Sweets
foodScene.note: Fresh coconuts, southern fruit, and coconut-milk desserts are easy to find at markets and roadside stalls, great for beating the midday heat.

attractions.name: Haad Rin
attractions.blurb: The twin beaches at the south of the island and the hub for hotels, restaurants, bars, and the Full Moon Party. Haad Rin Nok is lively, Haad Rin Nai is quieter.

attractions.name: Than Sadet–Koh Phangan National Park
attractions.blurb: The park holds Than Sadet waterfall, Phaeng waterfall, and the forest at the heart of the island. Take a short trek, swim under the falls, and see the royal initials carved in the rocks.

attractions.name: Bottle Beach
attractions.blurb: A quiet white-sand beach on the north coast, reached by boat or on foot. Clear water, few people, perfect for getting away from the bustle.

attractions.name: Koh Ma, Mae Haad
attractions.blurb: A small island linked to Mae Haad by a sandbar, and the best snorkeling spot on the island for coral. You can walk across the sandbar at low tide.

attractions.name: Dome Sila Viewpoint and Phaeng Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A hiking trail up the center of the island to the Dome Sila viewpoint, with views of the island and the sea all around, passing Phaeng waterfall where you can stop for a swim.

attractions.name: Haad Yao and the West-Coast Beaches
attractions.blurb: Haad Yao, Haad Son, and Srithanu beach on the west coast are spots for sunsets and quiet beachfront stays.

attractions.name: Srithanu Wellness Area
attractions.blurb: The west-coast district of yoga, spas, and health cafes. People stay long term to study yoga, recover, and live at a slower pace by the sea.

attractions.name: Thong Sala, Pier and Market
attractions.blurb: The island's main pier district, with a market, shops, banks, and a night market. It's the ferry hub and the starting point for getting around the island.

itineraryIdeas: Koh Phangan 3D2N — Haad Rin, Than Sadet, Bottle Beach
